newsitem.title: LATVIA: Gazprom, German firms to buy Latvian Gas stake.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom, German firms to buy Latvian Gas stake.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom and Germany's Preussen and Ruhrgas have agreed to pay 30 million lats for a stake in Latvian Gas, newspaper Diena quoted the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) on Friday as saying.
The two German firms will together buy a 16.25 percent stake, while Gazprom, separately, will purchase a further 16.25 percent holding.
The deadline for the payment is August 15, the newspaper quoted LPA director general Janis Naglis as saying.
The German companies had delayed the signing of a deal several times as they were worried by the debts of Latvian Gas.
But a government decision to cut the gas company's debts by some 30 million lats persuaded the Germans to agree to the deal.
The newspaper quoted Naglis as saying that talks with the German firms ended on Thursday during which the purchase of the shares and the share sale agreement were discussed.
